releases.name: Anka 1.0.1
releases.body:
**Anka 1.0.1** opens games stored as **.nup** packages.

Built from [`anka`](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/tree/anka) at `2d17a71ff0f0cf0c27b3d7207818fade9199b77b`; both programs carry this commit.

## Updating from 1.0.0

Close Anka, unzip **`Anka-1.0.1-win64.zip`** into your Anka folder and replace the files. Your `user` folder (settings, keys, firmware and saves) stays as it is.

New to Anka: follow the quick start in the [1.0.0 notes](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/releases/tag/anka-v1.0.0). Unzip into a new, empty folder, start `anka.exe`, and install your own keys and firmware.

## What's in 1.0.1

### .nup packages
- `.nup` ("Unencrypted (Archival) Package") is a container format from upstream Eglantine. It holds one title's base game, update and add-on content in a single file.
- Anka now **reads** .nup files. You can open them with **File › Load File…**, and they appear in the game list with their icon, name and version. `anka-cli.exe` and its launchers open them too, including from the `Games` folder.
- Mods (LayeredFS) and Anka's game-specific settings apply to games opened from a .nup, the same as for other formats. Anka finds the title ID before the game starts.

releases.name: Anka 1.0.0
releases.body:
First release of **Anka**, a Nintendo Switch 2 emulator for Windows, focused on performance.

Built from [`anka`](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/tree/anka) at `b7542ece8b5c695e2f01d5e46b74c0806d48ae96`; both programs carry this commit.

## Quick start

1. Unzip **`Anka-1.0.0-win64.zip`** into a **new, empty folder**. Do not unzip it into another emulator's folder: its Qt DLLs would replace that program's.
2. Start **`anka.exe`**. Anka keeps its settings, keys, firmware and saves in the `user` folder next to it (portable mode) and does not touch `%APPDATA%\eden` or other installs.
3. Install your own keys and firmware as with other Eden-based emulators. Anka includes no games, keys or firmware; only use what you legally own.
4. Settings: **Emulation › Configure… › Anka**. The first start picks *Recommended*, the setup we measured (with GPU Mode *Fast*, the default; it also turns Reactive Flushing off).

Coming from PokeDinner-Eglantine 2.0.0: back up its `nand` folder (your saves), then copy its `user` folder next to `anka.exe`.

Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with a current Vulkan driver. Qt and the Visual C++ runtime come with Anka.

Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64.AppImage, for 4K, 16K and 64K page kernels alike
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly with the Files app.

releases.name: FF7Recomp 1.1.63
releases.body:
**Fixed: party names and mini avatars gone with Battle+, and the battle help text gone after Tifa's or Cait Sith's reels, with Enhanced Stock UI (#93)**

Reported in issue #93, both with Enhanced Stock UI:

**Names and mini avatars disappeared when Battle+ was on.** Enhanced Stock UI's mini avatars borrow one byte of each character's saved data during a battle: the byte right before the name, which normally holds the Limit gauge. It puts the avatar there and draws the name from that byte, so the avatar shows up in front of the name. Battle+ kept that byte full (255) in battle too. In FF7's text, 255 means "end of text", so the name and the avatar were both empty. Battle+ now fills that saved gauge only outside battle. In battle it fills the battle's own gauge, as before, so Limits are still ready every turn.

releases.name: FF7Recomp 1.1.62
releases.body:
**Fixed: crashes in some scenes with Echo-S voices and ChaOS's Resized Models (#91)**

Reported in issue #91: with Echo-S 7's voices on, the game closed in some scenes, for example on boarding the Highwind from the world map.

Two mods were each changing half of the same scene. ChaOS's **BETA: Resized Models** option replaces the list of character models for 693 scenes, a list made to match the original game's scene scripts. Echo-S's voiced version brings its own scene scripts, and in 39 scenes those use more characters than ChaOS's list loads. In the Highwind's deck, for example, the scripts use 14 models and ChaOS's list has 10. The game then tried to animate a character that was never loaded and crashed on the first frame. (ChaOS's own description of the option warns that it can crash with gameplay mods.)

Now, when a mod's model list doesn't match the models the scene's scripts use, that list is left out for that scene, and the scene keeps the models that came with its own file. In those 39 scenes the characters have their normal size instead of ChaOS's resized one; everywhere else Resized Models works as before. The log (`ff7.log`) names each scene where this happens.

releases.name: v1.1.61
releases.body:
**Fixed: rare crashes at scene changes with sound-effect mods on (#90)**

Reported in issue #90: once in a while the game closed when entering a battle, leaving the menu, or moving between areas, more often with many mods on and little free memory. The crash records all showed the same thing: some other part of the app had a pointer whose lower half had been overwritten with zeros earlier on.

We tracked it down with a special memory-checking build on our test device, which caught it within a minute. The cause was in FFNx's sound-effect code, which is active whenever a mod replaces the game's sound effects (Echo-S, the Tsunamods set and others). It keeps one record per sound channel. Some calls used the wrong channel number, and every battle transition touched a channel that had no record. Each time, the game wrote a few bytes just past the end of that table, usually zeros, into memory that belonged to something else. Most of the time nothing happened; sometimes it hit a pointer, and whatever used that pointer next crashed.

releases.name: v1.1.60
releases.body:
**Fixed: the game could close a while after loading a save state from an earlier session (#91)**

Reported in issue #91 with Echo-S 7 voices on. The game keeps one data file open the whole time it runs: the sound archive it loads its own sound effects from. A save state stores the game's memory, and that memory held the open file's handle as it was in the session where the state was made. After you closed the game and loaded the state in a later session, that handle no longer pointed at anything. The next time a scene needed a sound the game hadn't loaded yet, the game crashed.

Whether you hit this depended on luck. It was more likely with mods that open many files, like Echo-S voices.

Save states now record which files the game has open, and opening them again is part of loading a state. States made with older versions are covered too: the sound archive is opened again when they load.

### Updating
Go to **Settings → Updates** in the launcher (or install this APK over your current version), then press **Play**. It asks to **Update the game** once (a few seconds).

APK SHA-256: `f29167fd9f2e8d88814386aacf28742669a42cc58810be4dca13f5972d3dd3ab`

releases.name: v1.1.59
releases.body:
**New: the launcher says what kind of device runs the game best, and what helps after a crash**

Suggested in issue #90. Rare crashes when a battle or scene is drawn for the first time are most often the phone running low on memory while the graphics driver prepares that scene's shaders. That is a hardware limit more than a bug, so the launcher now says so where you'll see it:

- **After the game crashes** (or Android closes it for memory), the launcher shows a short note once: what most often causes it, what helps, and a button to **Report a problem** if it keeps happening.
- **Report a problem** and **Game files** (first setup) show the recommendation.
- **Settings → Renderer** now recommends **OpenGL ES** on Mali GPUs (most MediaTek and Exynos phones).
- The README has the same line under *Playing*.

The recommendation: **8 GB of RAM or more, with other apps (browser tabs too) closed while you play.** Heavy mod sets need the most memory, above all on Vulkan. On Mali GPUs, OpenGL ES is usually the steadier choice.

![The note the launcher shows once after the game crashed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhuiyah/ff7-recomp-android/main/docs/release-images/1.1.59-crash-tip.jpg)

The first release since [0.3.0](https://github.com/FrankHUN88453/CoD3Recomp/releases/tag/v0.3.0): a faster game, a picture closer to the console's, and two experimental options that make it faster still.

## New

- **Faster on every level.** The emulated kernel woke every waiting thread whenever anything was signalled (one of the game's locks is released some 50,000 times a second); now only the threads waiting for that object wake. The game's CPU use dropped from about 5.4 cores to 3.3, and the forest at 1080p without MSAA went from about 91 to 95–108 frames a second.
- **Native command lists (experimental)**, in the F11 menu, after a restart. The draws are made from the game's own Direct3D calls, and the console's GPU command stream is run only for what the GPU still has to do. With **Watch memory writes (experimental)** also on, the forest at 1080p without MSAA runs at about 180 frames a second. Tested on eight levels, the films and mission restarts; off by default until it has been played more.

releases.body:
You need **Xbox360 Call of Duty 3 (USA, Europe).iso** file for install!

A fix release over [0.2.2](https://github.com/FrankHUN88453/CoD3Recomp/releases/tag/v0.2.2), and the one worth updating for: the lighting is right now.

## Fixed

**Walls lit far too brightly, and the odd shading on the soldiers and on the player's hands.** An instruction of the console's shaders has a vector half and a scalar half, and they run together: both read the registers as they were before the instruction and only then write. The translation wrote the vector's result first, so a scalar that read the very register the vector wrote got the new value instead of the old one.

The game's third light per surface is written exactly that way. Its scalar wants the specular exponent times a logarithm; with the write first it took a dot product instead, and two to the tenth of that became the specular. Every lit stone wall in Mayenne came out white with pink and green speckle, and characters were shaded oddly for the same reason. Eighty of the six hundred shader programs a level draws with have such an instruction, so this shows up all over the game, not only on that wall.

## Known issues

releases.name: Call of Duty 3 - PC Port - 0.2.2
releases.body:
You need **Xbox360 Call of Duty 3 (USA, Europe).iso** file for install!

A fix release over [0.2.1](https://github.com/FrankHUN88453/CoD3Recomp/releases/tag/v0.2.1); everything below is on top of what 0.2.1 brought.

## Fixed

**The HUD and the menu still flickered.** 0.2.1 looked at every texture every frame again, but a large one that had been still for a while was only *sampled*: sixty four places out of it. The HUD's fonts, icons and compass are small and change a handful of texels at a time, and the samples missed those changes, so the old picture stayed up for a frame. Everything up to two megabytes is now hashed whole, every frame, and only what is bigger than that falls back to sampling.

**Shadow filtering collapsed.** A texture fetch on the console carries three signed offsets in halves of a texel. The game's shadows are one map fetched four times at the corners of a texel; with the offsets dropped those were four fetches of the same texel, so a surface came out wholly lit or wholly dark instead of softly edged.

### Corrigido o crash na 1ª inicialização (selecionar ROM + Start Game fechava o app)
Na primeira execução do app, depois de selecionar a ROM e tocar em **Start Game**, o app fechava sozinho; na segunda inicialização funcionava perfeitamente. Causa raiz multi-fator, todas eliminadas:

## No more blinking objects after loading

While the game is running, each new combination of shader and render state needs a GPU pipeline. Pipelines the app has never seen are built in the background so the game doesn't freeze, and until one is ready the objects that use it are not drawn. Until now that also happened to pipelines it had already built in an earlier session. Only the first 4,000 were prepared at start-up, in the order they first appeared, so later in the game whole areas came from the background again. The result was objects and textures blinking for a few frames after loading a save or when walking into an area.

- Pipelines that the app has already built on your device are now created on the spot, in about a quarter of a millisecond each and within a small per-frame budget, so they are drawn from the first frame.
- Start-up preparation now begins with the pipelines your last session used (`pipelines_recientes.bin` in the game folder), not with the ones from the beginning of the game.
- Areas you visit for the very first time can still show an object a moment late while its pipeline is built. The second visit is clean.

releases.body:
Restores compatibility with third-party native mods. If mods failed to load, or loaded and then force-closed the game, this is the fix.

### Fixed

* **Mods failed to load with "Unknown mod load failure".** ([#6](https://github.com/igawa6/dusklight/issues/6))

  Adding the companion's slot I/II buttons pushed `BTN_R` to `1 << 8` and widened `daAlink_c::itemTriggerCheck` / `itemButtonCheck` from `u8` to `u16`. That changes the mangled names, so mods built against upstream Dusklight could not resolve them and failed at `dlopen`. The upstream symbols are re-exported as forwarders that translate the button numbering as well as the width — upstream's `BTN_B` is `BTN_S2` here, so widening alone would have routed a sword check to a slot button.

  Measured against three mods: only 2 of 842, 762 and 55 game-symbol imports were unresolved.

* **The game force-closed when a loaded mod ran.**

releases.name: Dual-Screen 3.0.1 (based on Dusklight v2.0.0)
releases.body:
Patch release for **Dual-Screen 3.0**. No gameplay or dual-screen changes — the native code is identical to 3.0.

### Fixed

* **Cosmetics, Luau Support and Randomizer were missing from the Android build.** ([#6](https://github.com/igawa6/dusklight/issues/6))

  The Android CMake presets listed only the `dusklight` target, so the `dusklight_mods` aggregate target never ran and `bundled_mods/` was never produced. Gradle packs that directory into `assets/mods`, so the APK shipped with no bundled mod packages at all. Mods that depend on the Luau runtime could not load either.

  All three packages are now present: `cosmetics`, `luau_runtime` and `randomizer`.

  CI was never affected — `build.yml` builds `dusklight_mods` as its own explicit `--target` step. This only broke preset-driven local builds.

# BachataS4 1.2.0

App Store: 1.2.0 (124), bundle games.bachatas4, interpreter only.
GitHub (sideload): BachataS4 JIT 1.2.0 (3), bundle games.bachatas4.jit.
Source: release-metal 4778beed8 (= metal-release-fixes).

## New
- Native Metal renderer, EXPERIMENTAL and off by default. Turn it on in Settings > Runtime >
  "Native Metal renderer (Experimental)". It applies from the next game launch. MoltenVK stays
  the default renderer. Metal has been tested on Bloodborne only. Some games may render wrongly or not start with Metal; switch it off if so.

## Performance
- MoltenVK queue submits are asynchronous on iOS: the emulator no longer waits on each submit.
- Metal shader compile workers run at utility QoS, so they compete less with the game threads.

## Fixes (Metal renderer)
- Write protection of pages a pending GPU write targets is held back; the GPU is waited for before wrapped guest pages are unmapped (God of War III boot fault).
- The copy-shader HLE drops elements past the destination buffer.
- Small read-only guest data is copied when a draw binds it.
- A buffer write skips the write-back of images it covers.
- A wait that a pending fence ends submits the queued GPU work.

- Added the ability to reinstall system files, allowing recovery even if the system files are accidentally damaged.

O jogo guarda a profundidade dos mapas de sombra em 16 bits (D16). O driver dos Huawei Maleoon recusava o D16 e fechava o jogo na abertura (#301). Por isso, desde a 0.4.0, o app usava D32 nesses aparelhos. Só que o D32 deixa cenas inteiras escuras: o céu fica certo, mas o terreno, as construções e os personagens quase pretos (#516). releases.name: BOTWRecompAndroid 0.4.13 (beta 45): correção para o travamento da Mali nas lutas
releases.body:
**Beta 45.** Uma correção para o travamento depois de alguns minutos de luta na Mali, e três mudanças de desempenho para a Mali.

## O travamento da Mali (#401)

Na Mali-G1 Ultra do #401, o jogo travava depois de alguns minutos de luta (com muitos efeitos), no modo Nativo e no Recompilado. Os logs mostravam uma thread do jogo presa percorrendo a lista de blocos livres do alocador de memória do jogo, que dava a volta.

- **A causa provável:** na Mali, o que um shader grava na memória do jogo é copiado de volta quando a GPU termina. Fora da "arena" de memória global, essa cópia era da faixa inteira, e desfazia o que o jogo tinha escrito ali no meio-tempo, inclusive os cabeçalhos e os links da lista de blocos livres, que ficam logo antes dos buffers. A 0.4.10 já fazia a cópia certa, mas só dentro da arena, que nunca liga nas Malis cujo driver oferece a importação de memória (como a G1 Ultra).
- **O que muda:** agora volta só o que a GPU mudou, palavra por palavra, e o que o jogo escreveu no meio-tempo fica. Quando isso acontece, o log diz `copy-back: a word the game wrote meanwhile kept`.

No game data is included: you need your own copy of the game (USA, S2LE01).

releases.body:
What's new in 0.78

For players
- **32-bit devices:** one APK now holds both ARMv8 (arm64-v8a) and ARMv7
  (armeabi-v7a). Android picks the right one on install, so 64-bit devices
  always run the 64-bit version. OpenGL ES 3.0 is still required.
- **Screen orientation:** the setting now applies to the launcher as well as
  the game and takes effect at once. Auto respects the system rotation lock.
- **Sound:** the audio buffer margin now adapts to the device.
- **Launcher:** new Advanced screen with a Debug mode switch. With it off,
  nothing is written to the log.
- **Logs:** new screen under Data to export, share or send logs to the
  developer, or clear them.

Under the hood
- **Most of the game is now ported C++:** - game code is moving from recompiled to ported native ARM code.
- **Old processor code removed:** x87 emulation is gone from the generated
  code, and the whole game runs in 24-bit floating point. MMX, CPU detection
  and the Pentium FDIV workarounds are removed too.

Known limits
- ARMv7 has only been tested in the 32-bit mode of a 64-bit phone, not on a
  real 32-bit device, so speed on older hardware is unknown.

releases.name: v0.77
releases.body:
What's new:

### For players
- **Dynamic Fullscreen for races.** A new Screen Size option that fits the race to your phone's shape (20:9, 16:9, tablets) with no black bars, you can find it in Resolution tabs in-game Graphics settings. The view widens to the sides and the HUD keeps its proportions. It is the default for new imports. 
- **Options on the first screen.** The "NFS Web Site" button is now "Options...", so the settings are one tap away.
- **Gamepads: Analog or Digital** (Controls → Gamepads). In Digital mode you steer with the D-pad and use the triggers for gas and brake, like a keyboard.
- **Force feedback: one choice, Off / Phone / Gamepad**, instead of two separate switches. The in-game Stick Volume slider now actually sets the vibration strength (it used to always be full).
- **Dead zone and saturation** from the game's own Dead Zone screen now work, separately for the stick and each trigger.
- **The demo movie no longer freezes** on its last frame.
- **Split screen** uses the Modern Patch layout.

### Under the hood (same behaviour, now native code instead of recompiled)

releases.name: v0.76
releases.body:
What's new:

- New launcher UI on Compose.
- Network races work: phone with phone over Wi-Fi (IPX or TCP/IP), and phone with a PC running the Modern Patch over TCP/IP, as host or client.
- Disc image import: the launcher reads the game straight from an ISO or BIN/CUE image, on the first start and on the Data screen.
- Faster and cooler: the renderer driver and about fifty of the game's heaviest functions now run as native code. Each was checked bit for bit against the original. Removed voodoo2a emulation wrapper - now GPU code is fully native OpenGLES. 
- Rear-view mirror like the main view: full draw distance, track detail, full-size cars, sky with clouds and lightning, car lights and headlights.
- Fixed bugs on certain devices with saves.

releases.name: The Sims 2 for Android 0.3.1-dev
releases.body:
The Sims 2 for Android **0.3.1-dev** improves Lua error handling, material creation, renderer diagnostics, texture conversion, and the launcher. Changes since **0.3-dev**, from signed source commit `a84f6585caca7a90afe140540714f879800c33bb`.

One APK includes **arm64-v8a** and experimental **armeabi-v7a**. The minimum requirements are now **Android 8.0 (API 26)** and **OpenGL ES 3.1**; the native Vulkan renderer accepts **Vulkan 1.0**. Game data must come from a compatible The Sims 2 Legacy Collection installation. Android 8.0–8.1 and GLES 3.1-only devices still need further device testing.

## Stability and startup

- Fixed the embedded MSVC `setjmp/longjmp` implementation used by Lua: returning to an error handler now unwinds the actual native call stack as well as restoring guest state. The bridge covers all 34 original setjmp call sites and both longjmp epilogues.
- Handle nested and repeated Lua errors, restore exception state, and remove jump contexts when their function returns, a C++ handler unwinds past them, or their thread ends. A jump to a function that has already returned is diagnosed.

releases.name: The Sims 2 for Android 0.3-dev
releases.body:
One APK now supports both **arm64-v8a** and experimental **armeabi-v7a**. The port requires Android 10 or later, OpenGL ES 3.2, and game data from a compatible The Sims 2 Legacy Collection installation. ARM32 also requires Thumb-2, NEON, and 4 KiB kernel pages. Android chooses the ABI, and the app unpacks the matching XZ-compressed engine on first use.

## Graphics and performance

- Fixed flickering and missing objects on Mali-G51 in OpenGL ES. The workaround defaults to on and can be changed in Advanced renderer settings. Fixed a related driver hang reproduced on Mali-T830.
- OpenGL ES compiles and links uncached shader programs in the background, reducing stalls when zooming out, rotating the camera, or changing floors.

### Added

  on Windows), and an error box instead of the window vanishing.

releases.body:
Xbox Live through Insignia, and game fixes.

### Xbox Live
- **Insignia** — Settings → Network → Connection → Xbox Live: Insignia connects the console to Insignia, the revival of the original Xbox Live: Live games sign in, find matches and play online. If your Internet provider blocks Insignia's DNS server, point it at a computer running insigniaDNS instead
- **Xbox Live setup** — Settings → Network → Xbox Live setup walks you through it, one step at a time: the connection, the Xbox dashboard, registering the console with Insignia's Setup Assistant (downloaded for you), then making or recovering your account in the dashboard
- **Dashboard** — the library's Dashboard button (top left) starts the Xbox dashboard from the console's hard disk, where Xbox Live accounts are made and recovered. The first time, it installs the dashboard from a zip of its files (dashboard 5960) that you provide: hakuX doesn't include one
- **Title updates** — a game's Xbox Live update, once downloaded, starts with the game. Forza Motorsport's 60 and 120 fps mods cover its update too

### Games
- **Fable: The Lost Chapters** — the hero's face and arms are no longer black or noise

releases.name: hakuX 1.2.0
releases.body:
System link, stability and compatibility improvements.

### Network
- **System link over your network** — Settings → Network → System link → LAN: hakuX devices on the same Wi-Fi network find each other as Xbox consoles on a LAN do. Devices the network's broadcasts don't reach, on another subnet or a VPN such as ZeroTier or Tailscale, are added by address under Other consoles
- **XLink Kai** — system link over the Internet through an XLink Kai engine running on a computer on your network; its web page picks the game's arena
- **Console identity** — each console has its own serial number, network address and online key. A device whose hard disk was copied from another one offers to make itself a new identity, since two consoles with one identity can't see each other


### Games
- **Sega GT 2002** — the cars have their paint, reflections and sun highlights
- **Doom 3** — no longer crashes as its main menu loads
- **Fatal Frame II** — starts and reads its disc in the order it asks for
- **AirForce Delta Storm** — answers the controller and the on-screen controls (it ignored all input)
- **Silent Hill 2** — no longer crashes when it loads a room

releases.name: hakuX 1.1.0
releases.body:
GPUs beyond Adreno (experimental).

### GPUs
- **Mali, Xclipse and PowerVR (experimental)** — hakuX runs on GPUs other than Adreno: features they lack are replaced (BC and 4444 textures decoded up front, standard border colours, the push block in a buffer, D32S8 depth), and known driver bugs are worked around (`hw/xbox/hle/vk/quirks.c`). Burnout 3 and Mercenaries run cleanly on a Pixel 8 (Mali-G715)
- **Vulkan 1.1 drivers** — GPUs whose drivers stop at Vulkan 1.1 (Valhall Mali on older or vendor-capped drivers, Qualcomm's own older drivers, early Xclipse, PowerVR BXM) run through a compatibility layer (`hw/xbox/hle/vk/compat.c`)
- **Older GPUs without descriptor indexing (experimental)** — Bifrost Mali (G71, G72, G76, G52) and PowerVR Rogue: each draw binds its own textures, and depth is clamped in the shader where the GPU can't
- **Adreno** — unchanged: every replacement is off where the GPU has the feature.

### App
- **GPU driver** — a screen of its own (Settings → GPU driver): the system driver and the stored packages in one list, with their versions and authors. Packages are checked when added and can be deleted (deleting the one in use goes back to the system driver)

releases.name: hakuX 1.0.0
releases.body:
A new core replaces xemu's QEMU-based one.

### New core
- **CPU** — the Xbox's x86 code runs on a FEX JIT (FEXCore fork), and the Xbox kernel is reimplemented natively (`native/kernel`): no QEMU
- **GPU** — the NV2A push buffer is decoded into Vulkan (HLE, `hw/xbox/hle`). Custom drivers (Turnip) load through adrenotools; driver-specific workarounds are quirks (`hw/xbox/hle/vk/quirks.c`, `debug.hakux.quirks`)
- **Audio** — the MCPX APU runs on the core's own services (`native/dev/apu`), out through AAudio
- **Savestates** — per game, in slots, with the hard disk's files
- **Mods and cheats** — per game, from `mods/` (library long-press "Mods & cheats"): XBE patches and replaced disc files; 60 and 120 fps mods for 13 games (`mods/README.md`, generators in `tools/mods`)
- **Controllers** — each physical controller routed to a player with its own mapping; the on-screen controller adds to player 1

### New features
- **Updates** — hakuX looks for a newer release on GitHub when it starts and on demand (Settings → Updates); one found shows its notes and installs from there
- **Frontends** — a game launched from ES-DE or another frontend returns to it when it closes

releases.body:
# SeedlessDS 1.1 正式版

版本名为 `1.1`，版本号为 `153`。本次同时发布原包名替换版、共存版、对应源码及 SHA-256 校验文件。两版均关闭 Android 调试标志，正式版本号与发布文件名均不含 debug，测试控制面板关闭。

## 本次改进

- 修复后台存档提前完成时，完成状态被模拟线程覆盖，导致后续快速存档和读档一直被忽略的问题。
- 减少存读档结束后的多余槽位查询、成就附加档读取和目录扫描，成就校验改为流式 SHA-256。
- 拆分即时存档、游戏电池存档和其它文件的访问锁，避免后台慢存档连带阻塞游戏文件读取。后台存档线程降低优先级。
- 防止并发慢查询重新发布已失效的目录列表，修复日志时间格式化的并发访问。
- 在应用私有目录保留有大小上限的近期存读档记录，便于追查偶发卡顿。
- 保留 SoundTouch 原声音高加速、低延迟音频恢复修复，以及按 RP Duo 上下屏实际画面尺寸适配的柔和颗粒、柔和颗粒＋和 Nova 磷光点滤镜。

## 安装包选择

| 文件 | Android 包名 | 安装方式 |
|---|---|---|
| `seedless-ds-1.1-coexist.apk` | `com.seedlessds.app.debug` | 可直接更新本分支旧共存版，也可与官方版共存 |
| `seedless-ds-1.1-replacement.apk` | `com.seedlessds.app` | 原包名替换版 |
| `seedless-ds-fork-1.1-src.zip` | — | 两版对应的完整源码与构建配置 |
| `seedless-ds-1.1-SHA256.txt` | — | 安装包和源码校验值 |

共存版按用户选择保留历史包名中的 `.debug`，以支持覆盖更新，应用本身已关闭调试。两版均沿用本分支旧签名。

替换版与官方版签名不同。首次换用替换版，请先导出存档与配置，再卸载官方版并安装。直接覆盖官方版会因签名不匹配而失败。两个包名的数据各自独立，切换使用时需导入存档。

两版均支持 ARM64，最低 Android 5.0。证书 SHA-256 为 `99e2395bd7c458a577e6bc4f4c7237a7474cb20a178fad07313c2778a7943165`，沿用仓库随源公开测试签名。

## 验证范围

- 两种正式构建各 128 项应用测试通过，完成构建、Lint、包名和签名检查，并核对 `debuggable=false`、`testOnly=false` 及 `BuildConfig.DEBUG=false`。两版的应用资源和原生库一致。
- 原生回归覆盖 21 类存档故障、280 轮重复存读档及请求交错。

```sh
sha256sum -c aether-install.py.sha256
```

# FusionHUD v1.1

Brings FusionHUD up to date with the HUD in [Bannerlator](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator) (main `b74261e6`). The HUD files are byte-identical copies of Bannerlator's, with only the license header added.

## New in the HUD
- **Pill size:** battery temperature as a `BAT °C` chip next to RAM, and a GPU name that is wider than the stats gets its own line across the top.
- **MediaTek GPUs:** GPU load and clock are read from MediaTek's GED nodes.
- **Charging state:** when Android reports no charge state, it is read from `/sys/class/power_supply` instead.
- **Config fix:** a config string with a single setting (for example just `hudSize=pill`) is no longer ignored.
- **Optional readouts your app can set** (nothing is drawn until you set them):
  - `setPresentedFps` — frames reaching the screen next to the game's own rate when something adds or drops frames after the game, e.g. `60→120` with frame generation or `60→45` when frames are lost.
  - `setDisplayServer` — `X11` or `Wayland`.
  - `setHdrState` — an HDR status line (`FusionHdr` codes).
  - `setGpuSpoofName` — the GPU name reported to games, marked "(spoof)" on the GPU row.

## Demo app

releases.name: FusionHUD v1.0
releases.body:
# FusionHUD v1.0

**FusionHUD** is a lightweight, forkable in-game performance overlay for Android (Winlator / Wine / PC-emulation projects) — the MangoHud-inspired HUD extracted from [Bannerlator](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator) so any project can adopt it.

## What you get
- **The Fusion HUD** — one overlay, **5 tap-cyclable sizes** (Full / Tiles / Pill / Minimal / Mega) with toggleable per-metric chips.
- **A hardened, cross-vendor metric backend** — FPS + frametime graph, CPU (aggregate + per-core), GPU %/clock/temp, thermals, RAM/VRAM, battery (with the **mA/µA current-unit auto-detect** that fixes `0.0W` on OEMs like HONOR), and network — with graceful fallbacks across **Adreno · Mali · PowerVR · Xclipse**.
- **Diagnostics export** for triaging metric gaps on unusual devices.
- Composited ~1 Hz off the present path — designed not to cost frames.

## How to adopt it
- **Gradle (JitPack):** add JitPack and depend on `com.github.The412Banner:FusionHUD:v1.0` — or grab the **`fusionhud-release.aar`** attached below.

The headline: the graphics translation makes simpler shaders, so the GPU does less work for every picture.

Pagurin catches up with nx2android's main branch of 2026-11-17. Three new settings, an audio output picker in the game's pause menu, and Android's Performance Game Mode.

Under Input, Menu button shows or hides the on-screen menu button (Back still opens the menu), and Controllers either gives each controller its own player or makes them all player 1. - Pagurin declares Android's Performance Game Mode. With Pagurin set to Performance, a game keeps its own frame rate instead of stepping down to 40 or 30.
- A game added with the import tool while Pagurin is open now shows its new settings and size right away. In 0.2.1 you had to reopen Pagurin.

releases.name: Pagurin 0.2.1
releases.body:
Pagurin catches up with nx2android's main branch of 2026-11-11: games can use local play over Wi-Fi, and a controller's face buttons can follow their labels.

## What's new

- **Local play over Wi-Fi.** Pagurin now has the network permissions a port's host asks for, so a game whose profile turns on local play (`DM_LAN`, such as Animal Crossing: New Horizons) can reach other players on the same Wi-Fi.
- **Face buttons setting.** A game's Input settings have a **Face buttons** row: **Position** (the Switch's layout, the default) or **Label** (A is the button marked A, as on an Xbox-style controller). It's the same setting as the pause menu's Face buttons row.
- **The import tool cleans up `sysdata/` too.** A port made with `--firmware` carries system data, and running the tool again now removes what an older port left there.

## Before you update

- The Face buttons row only shows for a port made from nx2android's main branch on 2026-11-09 or later. An older port doesn't read the setting, so the row stays hidden.

releases.name: Pagurin 0.2.0
releases.body:
GPU drivers now work the way nx2android's main branch takes them, and a game can be removed from the library.

## What's new

- **GPU drivers for nx2android's main branch.** Each game picks one of three:
  - **The game's own driver** (the default): the one its port was made with (`porter port --vulkan-driver`), or the system's if the port has none.
  - **The system driver**, even for a port that brought its own.
  - **A driver you added from a file.** Pagurin carries libadrenotools itself, so this also works for ports made without a driver.
- **Remove a game** from its settings tab. You choose whether to keep its save; a kept save is picked up again if you add the game back.
- **The import tool cleans up.** Running it again removes files an older port of the game left behind in `host/`, `mods/`, `RomFS/` and `aoc/`.
- The game page shows its button hints in the same order on every tab. LB and RB are on the tab bar.

## Before you update

- Choosing a driver needs a port made from nx2android's main branch on 2026-11-03 or later. An older port still runs, on the system's driver. Port it again to choose a driver.

The first release. Pagurin keeps your Android ports of games from other platforms in one app, such as those made with [nx2android](https://github.com/shirai91/nx2android), instead of a separate app per game.

## What's in it

- A library of your ports, with search and sorting.
- Settings for each game: docked or handheld mode, the on-screen gamepad, rumble, the frame rate counter and the engine's performance switches. A game only shows the settings its own host reads.
- One game language for every game. A game that doesn't have it runs in English.
- GPU drivers, added from a file and picked per game.
- Save export, import and delete. Import also takes another app's save folder or a zip.
- Games added from a PC with the import tool, or moved over from ports already installed as their own apps (AYN devices, or Shizuku elsewhere).

## Downloads

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Pagurin-0.1.0.apk` | The app. Android 10 or later, arm64. |
| `pagurin-import.exe` | The import tool for Windows. On other systems, run `tools/pagurin_import.py` with Python 3.9 or later. |

Pagurin catches up with nx2android's main branch of 2026-11-17. Three new settings, an audio output picker in the game's pause menu, and Android's Performance Game Mode.

## What's new

- Three settings for each game. Under Input, Menu button shows or hides the on-screen menu button (Back still opens the menu), and Controllers either gives each controller its own player or makes them all player 1. Under Performance, GPU turbo holds the GPU at its highest clock, always or only while frames run late.
- The pause menu's Game tab has an Audio output row. It sends the game's sound to the output you pick, such as the device speaker or Bluetooth headphones, until the game ends.
- Pagurin declares Android's Performance Game Mode. With Pagurin set to Performance, a game keeps its own frame rate instead of stepping down to 40 or 30.
- A game added with the import tool while Pagurin is open now shows its new settings and size right away. In 0.2.1 you had to reopen Pagurin.
- The group headings in a game's settings (Graphics, Input, Performance and so on) are in the app's accent colour, so the groups stand apart.
- The README is reorganised, with a Quick start first.
